global.headline: Anthropic says an unreleased Claude model built working exploit chains in five major platforms
global.source_title: Anthropic's Claude AI found ways to hack Chrome, Android, Windows and Linux
global.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says an unreleased internal Claude research model built complete, multi-step exploit chains against Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux after initial prompting. Anthropic says it reported every flaw to the vendors and describes only issues that have been fixed.
key_insights: Google assigned 62 CVEs to the Chrome issues, patched as of Chrome 156; 13 involved sandbox escapes.
The Linux flaw allowed zero-click remote root access via multipath TCP and has been fixed upstream and backported.
The findings come from Anthropic's own post and have not been verified by an independent party.
global.impact: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is now finding serious browser and OS flaws; users are protected only once they install the patched versions.

global.headline: New York Times and three US papers sue Brave over AI use of their journalism
global.source_title: Brave Faces Two Publisher Lawsuits Over AI Use of News Content
global.summary: The New York Times Company and the publishers of the New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune and Orlando Sentinel filed separate federal complaints against Brave Software on 2 November. They allege Brave copied and distributed their journalism through its search index, AI services and browser without permission.
key_insights: Each complaint brings five counts, including copyright infringement and circumvention of access controls under the DMCA.
The three newspapers' complaint was filed in the Southern District of New York.
No response from Brave was reported; the Times says two earlier letters to CEO Brendan Eich went unanswered.
global.impact: Brave's AI search and browser features now face a legal challenge from major US publishers; the outcome could shape how AI answer services use news content.

global.headline: OpenAI pledges its compute campuses will cut power use when grids are strained
global.source_title: OpenAI Launches Grid Protectors Program for Compute Campuses
global.summary: OpenAI launched a Grid Protectors Program under which its future compute campuses will reduce electricity use when grids are under strain, starting in Georgia. The first site, a planned campus in Effingham County, has an agreement for up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response.
key_insights: OpenAI says it will cover the full infrastructure and electric-service costs for the Georgia pilot.
How much demand is cut, how quickly and for how long will be set with utilities and regulators, and will vary by location.
OpenAI may use on-site generation, batteries and power controls where appropriate.
global.impact: Utilities and regulators weighing large AI data centres gain a working model for flexible demand, which could ease pressure on local grids.

global.headline: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve to prove which model weights produced an answer
global.source_title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve for Cryptographic AI Inference Proofs
global.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source research prototype that uses cryptographic proofs to show a model's response came from committed weights without revealing those weights. It is licensed under Apache 2.0 and labelled an unmaintained research artifact.
key_insights: Reported proof generation reaches 110 tokens per second for Meta's Llama 4 Maverick.
Proving a 24-request batch took about 223 seconds on one H100; CPU verification took about 17 seconds.
No independent security audit has been done, and proving used about 72 times the per-GPU time of FP8 inference.
global.impact: Auditors and customers could one day check that a provider served the model it claimed; for now the cost and lack of audit make it a research step.

india.headline: OpenAI says India is now ChatGPT's largest market by weekly users
india.source_title: ChatGPT India Largest Market, Says OpenAI MD
india.summary: OpenAI India managing director Prabhjeet Singh told The Economic Times that India is now ChatGPT's largest market by weekly active users, and that the user base has doubled since January 2026. The figures are OpenAI's own claim.
key_insights: Singh said OpenAI plans deeper localisation, Hindi and vernacular voice features, and UPI-linked payment announcements in the coming weeks.
Earlier market estimates put India's ChatGPT user base at about 100 million; Sam Altman had previously called India its second-largest.
india.impact: Indian users can expect more Hindi and regional-language voice features and UPI payments if OpenAI's planned announcements go ahead.

india.headline: IndiaMART puts its data behind logins to hold off Google AI search and AI agents
india.source_title: IndiaMART moves content behind logins to defend its data moat against Search and AI agents
india.summary: IndiaMART has moved content behind logins, blocked unrestricted scraping and restricted its data from Google Search and AI agents, MediaNama reported from the company's Q2 FY27 analyst call. CEO Dinesh Agarwal said the company is willing to give up 10-20% of unique business enquiries to protect its data.
key_insights: Unique business enquiries were 27 million in July–September, down 14% year on year.
Agarwal blamed Google AI Overviews, which he said now appear on 50% of searches or more.
IndiaMART is open to licensing redacted, non-personal data for AI training only if it earns revenue.
india.impact: Buyers may find fewer IndiaMART listings through Google and AI assistants as large Indian platforms start guarding their data from AI search.

india.headline: Google brings Dreambeans AI story app to India in 13 languages
india.source_title: Google Dreambeans India Launch in 13 Languages
india.summary: Google launched Dreambeans, an experimental AI app that turns a user's own digital activity into personalised illustrated stories, in India, its first market outside the United States. It supports 13 Indian languages alongside English on Android and iOS.
key_insights: With permission, the app draws on services such as Calendar, Gmail and Photos.
Languages include Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu and Bengali; users pick one language at a time.
No pricing was stated.
india.impact: Indian users get an early look at Google's personal-story AI in their own languages, which means granting it access to personal Google data.
